statuses.implemented: Discoverable implementation and tests exist with no specific known internal completion gap for this requirement; production activation may still require named external data.
statuses.partial: Some implementation exists, but a known internal gap, failing/unrun proof, contradiction, fixture-only path, or incomplete authoritative join remains.
statuses.unimplemented: No adequate repository implementation was found.
statuses.external-gated: Internal implementation is complete enough that only a registered external input or authorization remains.
statuses.historical: A delivery instruction or topology statement retained solely as provenance and superseded for current execution.

statusPolicy.rule: At repository-qualified review, partial and unimplemented are forbidden. Implemented means repository proof is complete; external-gated means repository proof is complete and only exact registered live input remains; historical is immutable provenance.
statusPolicy.mappingSemantics: Implementation arrays are evidence-discovery locators. Path-like values are exact repository paths; API/database values may be exact operations or objects; remaining human-readable labels are search terms to combine with the checked-in baseline manifests. A locator is not proof of completion, and exact executable test files remain discoverable through the tests baseline manifest where a row uses a suite label.
notes: The §22 five-lane plan and three historically named RC lanes are retained as provenance; main is the only active integration branch, repository qualification is complete, and this state does not declare an RC or launch.

Instance 1 baseline JSON blobs remain immutable in Git history and the verified pre-consolidation bundle; the checked-in manifests are the reproducible final consolidated-main inventory used for comparison. Final commit-addressed SHA, non-RC archival tag, all-refs bundle, restore output, and full timing transcript are emitted post-commit in the tag annotation and ignored archive manifest.
The canonical contract distinguishes the generated /v1 Hono contract from its browser-visible /api/v1 Next.js mount.
The canonical contract uses numeric(38,18), aligns Object Lock classes with ADR 0007, and includes all fifteen immutable artifact kinds.
Human design approval is a future user-entered RC/launch decision, is not claimed, and does not block repository qualification.
